about: The mosaic panel order's two copies held to one table (#412 item 1; spec 5.2, 2.4 PANELS).

server/astrodeck/sequence/panel_order.py orders the panels the run visits (order_panels, snake_index). The Target modal numbers its PANELS rows with a TypeScript copy of two of its keys, the snake index and least complete first (ui/src/components/flows/framing/sections/PanelsSection.tsx: snakeIndex, panelRows), because the modal has the progress route's counts and no visit times and no site.

server/tests/test_panel_order_fixture.py grades every case against order_panels and panel_order.snake_index; ui/src/components/flows/framing/__tests__/panelOrderFixture.test.ts grades the same cases against panelRows and snakeIndex. READ by both, never copied.
snake: a 0-based (row0, col0) in a grid cols wide and its snake index (compute_mosaic's panel list: even rows by ascending column, odd rows by descending).

cases: a grid of rows x cols, the panels the operator skipped (skip, 1-based [row, col]), and for every other panel its banked and total subs (panels, 1-based, total above 0), under one ORDER (order, the TARGET's option text; policy, to_plan.GROUP_ORDERS' reading of it). expect is the shot panels' labels in run order.

What the two copies share, and so what a case may hold: least complete first with NO visit times (fraction banked = banked / total, then the snake; ResumeArm orders the same way, 5.9) and grid order with NO last visit (the snake). Setting first is not shared: the modal lists it in grid order because the run orders it from the site (SETTING_FIRST_NOTE). A live panel with a total of 0 is not shared either: the modal reads its fraction as 0 and ResumeArm as 1.

cases.name: 3x2 on night one, least complete first: everything ties, so the snake decides (5.2's worked example)
3x2 on night one, grid order: the snake
3x2 part banked, least complete first: the fraction, then the snake among equals (1-2 before 2-2, 1-1 before 2-3)
3x2 part banked, grid order: the snake, the counts not read
3x3 with the first row done, least complete first: the rows behind it run the snake, the second row east to west
2x2 with 1-2 skipped, least complete first: the skipped panel is not ordered, and 1-1 and 2-1 tie at 3 of 9
a row of 3, least complete first: 2 of 6 and 1 of 3 are one fraction, so the snake breaks the tie
a column of 3, grid order: one panel per row, top to bottom
